【対象Topic】
Why Are More Cities Rethinking Public Benches?

【複数のSource(Claude Codeが既知URLへ直接アクセスして取得、またはWeb検索結果の要約として
取得したもの。それぞれのaccess_status/retrieval_methodを参照)】
[
  {
    "source_id": "SRC-001",
    "title": "Active Aging and Smart Public Parks",
    "authors_or_organization": "Boavida, J., Ayanoglu, H., Pereira, C.V., Hernandez-Ramirez, R.",
    "publication_date": "2023",
    "journal_or_venue": "Geriatrics, 8(5), 94",
    "doi": "10.3390/geriatrics8050094",
    "url": "https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10606855/",
    "source_type": "PRIMARY_JOURNAL_ARTICLE_REVIEW",
    "access_status": "FULL_TEXT_ACCESSIBLE_OPEN_ACCESS",
    "retrieval_method": "DIRECT_FETCH_KNOWN_URL_NOT_SEARCH",
    "fetched_extraction": "This is a literature review examining smart public parks' role in promoting active aging for older adults. Methodology: literature analysis of 28 recent articles (2020-2023) categorized by objectives, environmental aspects, solutions, methodologies, and geographic locations; search of the Elicit database used the phrase 'Smart parks for elderly wellbeing.' Key finding on seating: 'older users prefer a higher number of benches in public parks as they are inclined toward relaxation' (citing Stanley et al. within the review). Well-maintained parks featuring 'seating, pleasant paths, toilets, cafes' encouraged older visitors (citing Veitch et al. within the review). The reviewers recommend combining qualitative techniques (focus groups, interviews, observations) with objective measurements of comfort and usability to get more precise data on bench design. Geographic distribution of the 28 reviewed studies: European studies dominated (n=15), followed by Chinese research (n=5). Limitation: this was not a systematic literature review, so the authors state it cannot be guaranteed that all relevant information was fully covered."
  },
  {
    "source_id": "SRC-002",
    "title": "\"Benches become like porches\": Built and social environment influences on older adults' experiences of mobility and well-being",
    "authors_or_organization": "Ottoni, C.A., Sims-Gould, J., Winters, M., Heijnen, M., McKay, H.A.",
    "publication_date": "2016",
    "journal_or_venue": "Social Science & Medicine, 169, 33-41",
    "doi": null,
    "url": "https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/S0277953616304804",
    "source_type": "PRIMARY_JOURNAL_ARTICLE_QUALITATIVE_STUDY",
    "access_status": "ABSTRACT_AND_SECONDARY_SUMMARY_ONLY_PAYWALLED_FULL_TEXT",
    "retrieval_method": "WEB_SEARCH_AGGREGATED_SUMMARY_NOT_FULL_TEXT",
    "fetched_extraction": "Qualitative study using one-on-one seated and walk-along interviews with adults aged 60+ living in three adjacent neighbourhoods in Vancouver, Canada, at two time points (n=28 in 2012; n=22 in 2014). Findings: benches positively contributed to older adults' mobility experiences by enhancing their use and enjoyment of green and blue (waterfront) spaces, serving as a literal mobility aid (a place to rest during a walk), and contributing to social cohesion and social capital -- the paper's title concept is that benches function like a 'porch,' a semi-public perch that supports casual social contact in the neighbourhood. NOTE: full text was not accessible (paywalled); these facts are drawn from the published abstract and third-party summaries of the study, not from directly reading the full paper."
  },
  {
    "source_id": "SRC-003",
    "title": "Hostile architecture (encyclopedia article aggregating multiple primary/secondary sources on bench removal and defensive design)",
    "authors_or_organization": "Wikipedia contributors (aggregating cited academic and journalistic sources)",
    "publication_date": "accessed 2026-08-21",
    "journal_or_venue": "Wikipedia",
    "doi": null,
    "url": "https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hostile_architecture",
    "source_type": "TERTIARY_AGGREGATOR_WITH_CITED_PRIMARY_EXAMPLES",
    "access_status": "FULL_TEXT_ACCESSIBLE",
    "retrieval_method": "DIRECT_FETCH_KNOWN_URL_NOT_SEARCH",
    "fetched_extraction": "Explains why cities modify or remove benches as 'hostile' or 'defensive' architecture: cited claim that cities have 'a vested interest in eliminating signs of homelessness from communal spaces, fearing it might discourage investment from wealthier individuals' (article citation [20]); in England, the practice is described as stemming from 'a desire by the government to combat an anti-social street scene, taking the form of begging and street drinking' (citation [21]). Documented general techniques (treat as CATEGORIES, not tied to a specific confirmed incident below): sloped benches that require the user to support themselves with their feet, 'ubiquitous at bus stops across the United Kingdom' (citation [34]); center armrests that prevent lying down across a bench (citation [35]); 'Camden benches,' concrete-block benches designed to discourage sleeping, skateboarding, and sticker-placement (citation [36]); outright removal, which Fredrik Edin (cited, [57]) describes as 'the most common form of exclusionary design, in which... benches used by the public are removed precisely because the public uses them.' Important limitation explicitly noted in the article: as of March 2020, 'no wide-scale empirical study has been conducted to measure the impact of hostile architecture on the wellbeing of homeless people or other targeted populations' (citation [63]). CORRECTION (2026-08-21, after production Writer Fact Check independently re-verified the named incidents below via live web search against contemporaneous reporting): the specific named incidents originally drawn from this Wikipedia article (Stockholm Central Station bench removal 'in 2015', Lulea iron-bar benches, and the Malmo tilted-bench date/intent) did NOT hold up to primary-source verification and must NOT be used as confirmed facts. See SRC-004 for the corrected, fact-checker-verified version of the Malmo and NYC examples, which ARE usable."
  },
  {
    "source_id": "SRC-004",
    "title": "Production Writer Fact Checker's independent live-web-search corroboration of specific named hostile-architecture incidents (Malmo tilted bench, NYC subway bench removal post)",
    "authors_or_organization": "Findings surfaced by er003_v1_n3_01_articles_generate.py's production Fact Check gate (r3.run_fact_checker_with_gates), which has live web_search access; original reporting: Sveriges Radio, Aftonbladet",
    "publication_date": "cross-checked 2026-08-21 against contemporaneous 2010-2011 and 2021 reporting",
    "journal_or_venue": "sverigesradio.se; aftonbladet.se (as identified by the Fact Checker's own search)",
    "doi": null,
    "url": "https://www.sverigesradio.se/artikel/4382816",
    "source_type": "SECONDARY_JOURNALISTIC_CONTEMPORANEOUS_REPORTING_VIA_FACT_CHECK_GATE",
    "access_status": "SUMMARY_ONLY_SURFACED_BY_DOWNSTREAM_FACT_CHECKER_NOT_DIRECTLY_FETCHED_BY_RESEARCH_STAGE",
    "retrieval_method": "DOWNSTREAM_FACT_CHECK_WEB_SEARCH_NOT_RESEARCH_STAGE_RETRIEVAL",
    "fetched_extraction": "Malmo (Triangeln station, opened December 2010): a sloped/tilted bench design drew public complaints; the earliest confirmable contemporaneous report of a formal complaint to Sweden's Equality Ombudsman (DO) is dated 2011-03-04 (exact 2010 complaint date not independently confirmable). Importantly, a city official's 2011 explanation (per the Fact Checker's sourced summary) was that the bench had been ordered WITH a back and armrests specifically for accessibility reasons, but the seat that was delivered turned out to be more steeply tilted than intended, and the angle was subsequently corrected -- i.e., contemporaneous reporting describes this as an accessibility-design bench that came out more uncomfortable than planned and was then fixed, not a bench that was deliberately designed from the outset to be hostile. Some later commentators/researchers have nonetheless cited it as an example of sleep-deterrent design; the sources disagree on original intent. NYC Subway: a 2021 post from an NYC Transit official social-media account stated benches were being removed to stop homeless people from sleeping on them; the post was later deleted, and the MTA said it had been posted in error. This is a real, documented, dated public incident (a genuine example of the topic's social tension), but it should be presented as a since-retracted social-media statement, not as evidence of an adopted formal removal policy."
  }
]

evidence_items.source_location: fetched_extraction; park-features finding, citing Veitch et al.

evidence_items.evidence_summary: The reviewers recommend combining qualitative methods—focus groups, interviews, and observations—with objective measurements of comfort and usability to obtain more precise data on bench design.
evidence_items.supported_fact_category: recommended evaluation methods for bench design
evidence_items.population: older park users and public-park environments
evidence_items.causal_strength: Methodological recommendation, not an outcome estimate.

evidence_items.evidence_summary: Among the 28 reviewed studies, European studies dominated, followed by Chinese research.
evidence_items.population: studies of smart parks and older-adult wellbeing
evidence_items.causal_strength: Descriptive distribution only.
evidence_items.limitation: The review was not systematic and may not include all relevant studies.

evidence_items.evidence_summary: Publication metadata identifies the article as a 2023 review by Boavida, Ayanoglu, Pereira, and Hernandez-Ramirez, published in Geriatrics, volume 8, issue 5, article 94.
evidence_items.causal_strength: Bibliographic fact.

evidence_items.evidence_summary: This qualitative study investigated how the built and social environment influenced mobility and wellbeing among adults aged 60 and older living in three adjacent Vancouver neighbourhoods.
evidence_items.causal_strength: Qualitative observational/interview evidence; supports reported experiences rather than population-level causal inference.
evidence_items.limitation: Full text was inaccessible; the extraction is based on the published abstract and third-party summaries.
evidence_items.ambiguity: 二次要約由来、原文未確認。

evidence_items.evidence_summary: The study used one-on-one seated interviews and walk-along interviews at two time points. The sample was n=28 in 2012 and n=22 in 2014.
evidence_items.supported_fact_category: sample size, methods, and study period
evidence_items.numeric_scope: participants at each reported time point
evidence_items.population: adults aged 60+ in three adjacent Vancouver neighbourhoods
evidence_items.causal_strength: Descriptive qualitative evidence.
evidence_items.limitation: The extraction does not clarify whether the two samples were identical participants or separate samples.
evidence_items.ambiguity: 二次要約由来、原文未確認。参加者の重複状況は抽出テキストから不明。

evidence_items.evidence_summary: Participants reported that benches enhanced their use and enjoyment of green spaces and waterfront spaces, provided a literal mobility aid as places to rest during walks, and supported social cohesion and social capital.
evidence_items.supported_fact_category: reported benefits of benches for mobility and social wellbeing
evidence_items.causal_strength: Participant-reported qualitative association; not a controlled causal finding.
evidence_items.limitation: The extraction provides no quantitative effect estimate and full text was not accessed.
evidence_items.ambiguity: 二次要約由来、原文未確認。

evidence_items.evidence_summary: The paper’s “benches become like porches” concept describes benches as semi-public places that support casual social contact within a neighbourhood.
evidence_items.causal_strength: Interpretive qualitative finding based on the paper’s title concept and reported summaries.
evidence_items.ambiguity: 二次要約由来、原文未確認。

evidence_items.evidence_summary: Publication metadata identifies the study as a 2016 article by Ottoni, Sims-Gould, Winters, Heijnen, and McKay in Social Science & Medicine, volume 169, pages 33–41.
evidence_items.causal_strength: Bibliographic fact.
evidence_items.limitation: The DOI was not provided in the source metadata.
evidence_items.ambiguity: Full text paywalled; metadata and findings were accessed through the abstract/secondary summaries.

evidence_items.evidence_summary: The encyclopedia article describes hostile or defensive architecture as a reason cities modify or remove benches. It reports a cited claim that cities may seek to eliminate visible signs of homelessness from communal spaces because they fear such signs could discourage investment from wealthier individuals.
evidence_items.supported_fact_category: stated institutional/economic rationale for bench modification or removal
evidence_items.population: people experiencing homelessness and users of communal spaces
evidence_items.causal_strength: Cited claim summarized by a tertiary source; not an independently verified causal finding.
evidence_items.limitation: Wikipedia aggregates other sources, and the underlying citation was not supplied in the extraction.
evidence_items.ambiguity: 三次情報による要約。原引用の内容・文脈はこの抽出テキストだけでは確認できない。

evidence_items.evidence_summary: For England, the article describes defensive design as stemming from a government desire to combat an “anti-social street scene,” including begging and street drinking.
evidence_items.supported_fact_category: governmental rationale described for defensive design
evidence_items.numeric_scope: England, as described in the article
evidence_items.population: people involved in begging or street drinking and other public-space users
evidence_items.causal_strength: Description of a stated rationale; no policy-effect measurement is provided.
evidence_items.limitation: Tertiary aggregation; the underlying source and exact policy scope are not included in the extraction.
evidence_items.ambiguity: 三次情報による要約、原引用未確認。

evidence_items.evidence_summary: The article lists categories of exclusionary bench design: sloped benches requiring users to support themselves with their feet, center armrests that prevent lying across a bench, “Camden benches” designed to discourage sleeping, skateboarding, and sticker placement, and outright bench removal.
evidence_items.supported_fact_category: types of defensive or exclusionary bench design
evidence_items.numeric_scope: general categories described by the article
evidence_items.population: bench users, including people who may sleep on benches
evidence_items.causal_strength: Descriptive classification; does not establish how widespread or effective each technique is.
evidence_items.limitation: The extraction explicitly says these should be treated as categories, not as confirmed specific incidents.
evidence_items.ambiguity: 三次情報による要約。個別の実施場所・頻度・効果は確認できない。

evidence_items.evidence_summary: The article states that outright removal is described by Fredrik Edin as the most common form of exclusionary design when public benches are removed because the public uses them.
evidence_items.population: users of public benches, including potentially excluded groups
evidence_items.causal_strength: Quoted characterization by a cited commentator; not a measured prevalence estimate.
evidence_items.limitation: The extraction does not provide independent data supporting the claim that removal is the most common form.
evidence_items.ambiguity: 三次情報を介した引用。元発言・調査データは原文未確認。

evidence_items.evidence_summary: As of March 2020, the article states that no wide-scale empirical study had measured the impact of hostile architecture on the wellbeing of homeless people or other targeted populations.
evidence_items.numeric_scope: state of the cited empirical literature at that time
evidence_items.population: homeless people and other targeted populations
evidence_items.causal_strength: Explicit limitation statement about the evidence base.
evidence_items.limitation: This is a statement in a tertiary article and does not establish that no later study exists.
evidence_items.ambiguity: 三次情報による要約。基礎文献の確認範囲は不明。

evidence_items.evidence_summary: The article’s originally named examples involving Stockholm Central Station, Lulea, and Malmo were later flagged as not holding up to primary-source verification and must not be treated as confirmed facts.
evidence_items.supported_fact_category: verification status of specific hostile-architecture incidents
evidence_items.numeric_scope: specific incidents named in the encyclopedia article
evidence_items.causal_strength: Verification warning, not a substantive finding.
evidence_items.limitation: The extraction does not provide the full primary-source verification record.
evidence_items.ambiguity: The source itself records a correction; named incidents should be excluded unless supported by SRC-004 or another verified source.

evidence_items.evidence_summary: At Malmo’s Triangeln station, opened in December 2010, a sloped or tilted bench design generated public complaints. The earliest confirmable contemporaneous report of a formal complaint to Sweden’s Equality Ombudsman is dated 2011-03-04.
evidence_items.numeric_value: Station opened December 2010; formal complaint report dated 2011-03-04
evidence_items.population: bench users and members of the public raising accessibility concerns
evidence_items.causal_strength: Documented contemporaneous-reporting summary; does not prove deliberate hostile intent.
evidence_items.limitation: The source is only a downstream fact-check summary, not directly fetched primary reporting.
evidence_items.ambiguity: 二次要約由来、原報道原文未確認。

evidence_items.evidence_summary: A 2011 city-official explanation, as summarized by the fact checker, said the bench had been ordered with a back and armrests for accessibility; the delivered seat was more steeply tilted than intended, and its angle was subsequently corrected.
evidence_items.supported_fact_category: alternative accessibility explanation and correction of the Malmo bench
evidence_items.population: bench users, particularly people affected by accessibility and comfort
evidence_items.causal_strength: Contemporaneous explanation summarized by a fact checker; supports unintended design error more than deliberate exclusion.
evidence_items.limitation: The original reporting was not directly accessed in the research stage.
evidence_items.ambiguity: 二次要約由来、原文未確認。Sources reportedly disagree with later interpretations of original intent.
evidence_items.source_location: fetched_extraction; city-official explanation of Malmo design

evidence_items.evidence_summary: A 2021 post from an NYC Transit official’s social-media account stated that subway benches were being removed to stop homeless people from sleeping on them. The post was later deleted, and the MTA said it had been posted in error.
evidence_items.supported_fact_category: documented public controversy over bench removal
evidence_items.population: people experiencing homelessness and subway users
evidence_items.causal_strength: Supports the existence of a public statement and subsequent retraction; does not establish an adopted formal removal policy.
evidence_items.limitation: The post was deleted, and the MTA characterized it as erroneous.
evidence_items.ambiguity: 二次要約由来、原文未確認。Must be presented as a retracted social-media statement, not as confirmed official policy.

evidence_items.evidence_summary: The Malmo and NYC examples were independently surfaced by a downstream production fact-check gate using live web search, with original reporting identified as Sveriges Radio and Aftonbladet.
evidence_items.numeric_scope: specific named incidents discussed in SRC-004
evidence_items.causal_strength: Corroboration of incident reporting; not independent primary research.
evidence_items.limitation: The research-stage extraction contains only the fact checker’s summary and not the full articles.
